title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow

items.stem: What is the key difference between a workflow and an agent?

options.text: An agent can call tools, but a workflow can only call a model
A workflow needs a smaller model, but an agent needs a larger one
In a workflow, code fixes the path; in an agent, the model picks the next step
An agent remembers earlier requests, but a workflow starts fresh every time

items.stem: A makerspace assistant handles every question the same way: the program searches the manuals for the question text, pastes the top three pages into a prompt, and calls the model once to write the answer. How should this design be described?

options.text: An agent, because a language model writes the final answer
A workflow, because the program fixes every step in advance
An agent, because it looks up information outside the model
Neither, because it makes only one call to the model

items.stem: For a booking request, a fixed workflow always makes 2 model calls, while an agent loop averages 5 model calls. Assume every model call costs $0.01. Over 1,000 booking requests, how many more dollars does the agent cost than the workflow?
Which makerspace task is the best candidate for a fixed workflow rather than an agent?

options.text: Finding out why a student's 3D prints keep warping, using manuals and booking history
Recommending a machine for an unusual project the student describes in their own words
Answering a question that may need pages from several manuals and a follow-up lookup
Booking a laser cutter slot once the student has given the machine, date and time

items.stem: In a few words, what can an agent do that a fixed workflow cannot?

At a design review, a teammate proposes making the whole assistant one agent. Booking always follows the same three steps, but manual questions vary a lot. Which response is best supported by who owns the control flow and by cost?

options.text: Use a fixed workflow for booking and an agent only for open-ended manual questions
Use one agent for everything, since a model can follow the booking steps too
Use fixed workflows for everything, since workflows are always cheaper than agents
Use one agent for everything, since the booking steps then become more reliable
